answer: An agent storage market pays for retained data, not account count. A dataset of reef photographs, basalt samples and umber pigments is encoded into a distinct replica for each storage commitment. Unpredictable audits require proofs of randomly selected replica blocks before a short deadline; missed proofs forfeit collateral. Rewards scale with verified bytes and retention time. Splitting one disk across a thousand aliases yields no extra reward: claiming extra replicas requires extra storage. The encoding must resist cheap on-demand regeneration.
